title: OSMM Design System Object
description: Durable, foundational Context: how a brand LOOKS — its visual identity, color, typography, imagery, iconography, motion, layout, accessibility standards, rights, and the constraints governing what a generative system may produce with the identity. Canonical schema for object_type 'design_system'. The osmm-design-system-builder skill references this file; it is the single source of truth for the object's shape. Design System is the visual counterpart to Brand Context (which owns the verbal identity); the two pair one-to-one.

osmm_version.description: OSMM schema version this instance conforms to (semantic version).

design_system_id.description: Stable, human-readable id. Prefix 'DSY-' + lowercase hyphen slug, normally the same slug as the paired Brand Context. Never changes once assigned.

version.description: Instance version (e.g. '1.0'). Bump on revision; the id stays stable.

name.description: The design system's name as the organization calls it (e.g. 'IBM Design Language'). Falls back to '<Brand> Design System' when it has no formal name.

linked_brand_context.description: Id of the paired Brand Context Object (the verbal identity). Use 'BRC-PLACEHOLDER-<slug>' until it exists. Strongly recommended — the pair is the full identity.

linked_business_context.description: Optional. Id of the owning Business Context Object. Use 'BIZ-PLACEHOLDER-<slug>' until it exists.

owner.description: Optional. The team or role that owns and approves changes to this system (e.g. 'Brand Studio', 'Design Systems team'). Design systems have a different owner and change cadence from the verbal brand; recording it prevents unattributed drift.

design_principles.description: 3-6 durable visual principles — how the system decides, not what it contains. Principles, not adjectives: 'Type carries the hierarchy; color never has to' beats 'clean'.

identity.description: The logo and identity system: marks, lockups, and the rules protecting them.

primary_mark.description: The primary logo/mark: what it is and its canonical form.

mark_variants.description: Optional. Approved variants (monochrome, reversed, stacked, icon-only, wordmark) and when each is used.

lockup_rules.description: Optional. How the mark locks up with sub-brands, taglines, or product names.

clear_space.description: Optional. Minimum clear space around the mark, expressed in the system's own unit (e.g. 'the height of the wordmark's cap').

minimum_size.description: Optional. Minimum reproduction size, digital and print.

misuse_rules.description: Optional. Explicit don'ts (stretch, recolor, add effects, place on busy imagery). High value for generative use — these are the rules a model breaks first.

co_branding_rules.description: Optional. How the mark appears alongside partner, sponsor, or acquired brands — order, scale, separator, endorsement language.

color.description: The color system: semantic roles first, raw values second.

palette.description: The core palette. Capture the semantic role, not just the swatch — a downstream generator needs to know what a color is FOR.

token.description: Optional. The token name in the upstream source (e.g. '$blue-60', 'color.brand.primary').

name.description: Human name of the color (e.g. 'IBM Blue 60', 'Wendy's Red').

value.description: Optional. The value as published — hex, RGB, Pantone, or CMYK.

role.description: Optional. Semantic role: primary, secondary, accent, surface, text, border, success, warning, error, etc.

usage_notes.description: Optional. Where it may and may not be used.

usage_rules.description: Optional. Proportion/dominance rules, permitted pairings, and forbidden combinations. This is what keeps an accent color from becoming the brand color.

modes.description: Optional. Supported color modes (light, dark, high-contrast) and how the palette shifts across them.

typography.description: The type system: faces, their licenses, the scale, and the rules.

typefaces.description: The typefaces in the system. Licensing is not optional detail — an unlicensed face is a legal exposure and a production blocker.

role.description: Optional. What it sets: display, headline, body, UI, monospace, legal.

license.description: Optional. License terms and scope (open source, desktop-only, web seats, per-domain). Flag what is NOT covered.

fallback_stack.description: Optional. The web/system fallback stack when the licensed face is unavailable.

type_scale.description: Optional. The scale by role rather than by pixel guess.

token.description: Optional. Token name in the upstream source.

role.description: The role this step serves: display, h1, h2, body, caption, legal.

usage_rules.description: Optional. Pairing rules, hierarchy rules, alignment and case conventions, and what the system never does (e.g. 'never set body copy in the display face').

imagery.description: Optional but strongly encouraged. Photographic art direction — the fastest way for generated visuals to go off-brand.

art_direction.description: Optional. One paragraph: the photographic point of view.

subject_matter.description: Optional. What the brand photographs (real customers, product in use, empty environments).

treatment.description: Optional. Color grading, lighting, crop, depth of field, filters, overlays.

sourcing.description: Optional. Commissioned vs. stock vs. UGC vs. generative, and which is permitted where.

representation.description: Optional. How people are represented — casting, diversity, accessibility, and consent standards.

style.description: Optional. Icon style: geometry, stroke weight, corner treatment, fill vs. line, grid.

source.description: Optional. The canonical icon set and where it lives.

illustration_style.description: Optional. Illustration style and when illustration is used instead of photography.

usage_rules.description: Optional. Sizing, alignment, color application, and mixing rules.

motion.description: Optional. The motion system — increasingly load-bearing for social, CTV, and product UI.

principles.description: Optional. How the brand moves (e.g. 'motion clarifies cause and effect; it never decorates').

durations.description: Optional. Standard durations and when each applies.

usage_rules.description: Optional. Transition conventions, logo animation rules, reduced-motion behavior.

grid.description: Optional. The grid system (columns, gutters, margins) and how it adapts.

spacing_scale.description: Optional. The spacing scale and its base unit.

composition_principles.description: Optional. Composition rules: hierarchy, density, whitespace, safe areas.

accessibility.description: Optional but strongly encouraged. The standard the system holds itself to. A generator will silently violate whatever is not written down here.

conformance_target.description: Optional. The target standard and level (e.g. 'WCAG 2.2 AA').

contrast_requirements.description: Optional. Minimum contrast ratios for text, large text, and UI components.

minimum_type_size.description: Optional. Minimum legible type size by medium.

requirements.description: Optional. Other standing requirements: alt text, captions, focus states, color-independent meaning, reduced motion.

channel_specs.description: Optional. Durable, brand-level format rules per channel — aspect ratios, safe zones, minimum sizes. Distinct from Creative Strategy's channel_creative, which is the campaign-scoped creative treatment.

channel.description: The channel or medium (paid social, email, OOH, CTV, packaging).

specifications.description: Optional. The durable specs and constraints for that surface.

brand_architecture_rules.description: Optional. How the system flexes for sub-brands, endorsed brands, acquisitions, regions, and partnerships.

localization_rules.description: Optional. Script coverage, RTL behavior, substitute faces for non-Latin scripts, and regional color or symbol meaning.

rights_and_licensing.description: Optional. Usage rights that expire or restrict. The field nobody models and everybody gets burned by.

asset_type.description: What the right covers (typeface, photography library, music, talent, illustration).

terms.description: Optional. The scope of the grant and its limits.

expires.description: Optional. Expiry or renewal date, if the right is time-bound.

generation_constraints.description: Optional but the reason this is an OSMM object rather than a linked PDF: what a generative system may and may not produce with this identity.

generative_imagery_permitted.description: Optional. Whether AI-generated imagery may be used in brand-facing work at all.

permitted.description: Optional. What generation is explicitly allowed to do.

prohibited.description: Optional. What generation must never do (regenerate the logo, invent palette colors, synthesize a spokesperson).

style_descriptors.description: Optional. Model-safe descriptors of the visual style, for prompting.

negative_prompts.description: Optional. Descriptors to steer away from.

human_review_required.description: Optional. Cases that must clear human review before publication.

token_sources.description: Optional. Pointers to the upstream machine-readable token source. OSMM carries the semantic layer and REFERENCES the raw tokens rather than mirroring them.

type.description: Optional. The kind of source (W3C DTCG token file, Figma variables, Style Dictionary, Tailwind config, npm package).

name.description: Optional. Human name of the source.

reference.description: URL, repository path, or file identifier.

source_version.description: Optional. The version of the upstream source this object was built against.

asset_sources.description: Optional. Where the actual assets live. OSMM never holds binaries.

type.description: Optional. The kind of source (DAM, Figma library, Storybook, component package, brand portal).

name.description: Optional. Human name of the source.

reference.description: URL, repository path, or system identifier.

access_notes.description: Optional. Who can access it and how.

source.description: One line: what source(s) this was built from and approximate date.
